["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a week ago, review=Feast & Fable is the newest addition to Andheri West’s dining scene, already turning heads with its well reviewed food and thoughtfully designed aesthetic space. Conveniently located at just a short walk from Link Road or Metro stations, the place is easy to spot, with warm lighting and lush greenery that instantly draw you in.

The establishment is modern and chic, with open seating curated with a green, refreshing ambiance. It also offers an air-conditioned section featuring ambient lighting and a minimalistic design. The stacked bar looks great tucked into a corner, overlooking a comfortable sofa setup ideal for larger groups. The overall feels are chill, gram-worthy, and genuinely perfect for a date or family meet-ups.

We visited for a midweek dinner and to our surprise, the place already had a decent crowd, so a reservation is recommended. The staff was courteous and professional, and they offered us a nice table.

The pop playlist was soft, and we quickly got chatting while browsing the beautifully designed cocktail menu. The food menu lists down the ingredients and features a mix of Indian, Asian, and continental dishes, while the servers were always at hand to describe each item, making it much easier to order. We sampled :

-Virgin Mojito : Standard but well made. Arrived promptly. Apt choice to pair with starters.

-Ghost Chilli Chicken : Delicious and succulent, the chicken was char grilled to perfection. Served with a mango based chutney. Not as spicy as the name suggests.

-Spinach, Chilli & Ricotta Stuffed Mushrooms : Button mushrooms stuffed with fresh ricotta and spinach served on a bed of chilli tomato puree. Filling and crafty, the green apple and cinnamon chutney brings out the flavours.

-Spicy Prawns Tempura : Classic tempura, good size and crunch. Dynamite sauce does the trick.

-Mercado Verduras : Thin base with exotic toppings like sundried tomatoes, brocolli and olives. Rocket leaves sprinkled on top adding freshness and texture but may not be everyone's cup of tea.

-Black Pepper Rice Bowl : Sticky rice served with black pepper prawns gravy with a kick. Savoury aftertaste lingers for a while. Portion good enough for two.

The restaurant has a colorful and desi-style décor that immediately gives you a vibrant, festive vibe. The seating is comfortable and well spaced, making it a good place for family dinners or outings with friends. The overall atmosphere feels warm and welcoming, which adds to the dining experience.

Coming to the food, it’s quite impressive. The flavors are rich and authentic, and the portions are generous. Their curries, kebabs, and tandoori dishes stand out for their taste and presentation. The food definitely lives up to Urban Tadka’s reputation for good quality and traditional Indian flavors.

However, one thing that needs improvement is the service. The staff seemed a bit slow, and it took longer than expected for the food to arrive. Even after placing the order, getting follow-ups or additional items required some waiting. The service could be more attentive and prompt to match the great food quality.

Overall, Urban Tadka is a good restaurant for tasty food and a cheerful ambience, but if they work on their service speed, it would easily become one of the best dining options in Korum Mall., name_person=ashish Singh}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Dietary_restrictions, E:OTHER_DIETARY_RESTRICTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING, Kid-friendliness, E:KID_FRIENDLINESS, Wheelchair_accessibility, E:ACCESSIBILITY], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Not sure, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,400–1,600, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Very quiet, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Paid_parking_lot, E:PARKING_OPTION_PAID_PARKING_LOT], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Vegetarian_menu_or_section, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_SEPARATE_MENU_SECTION]}, time_line=4 months ago, review=Recently had both lunch and dinner at Urban Tadka, and it was an experience worth sharing. The moment you step in, the rustic desi vibe hits you — vibrant interiors, quirky signage, and that unmistakable aroma of rich Indian spices. The ambience strikes the perfect balance between traditional and modern, making it feel warm yet energetic.

Whether it’s a family lunch or a fun dinner with friends, it’s a place that brings you the joy of Indian food with a touch of desi drama., name_person=Saathvik Ganesh}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,400–1,600, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Masala_Papad, Corn_Kurkure], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=7 months ago, review=Visited Urban Tadka at Korum Mall recently and had a lovely dining experience overall.
The Hara Bhara Kabab was absolutely delicious — perfectly spiced, cooked just right, and served beautifully. Each bite was full of flavor and freshness.
We also tried the Jamun Lemon Soda, which was refreshingly tangy with just the right balance of sweet and sour — a perfect cooler.
Another highlight was the Corn Kurkure — super crispy, well-seasoned, and thoroughly enjoyable as a starter.

However, the Aloo Chana Biryani was a bit of a letdown. It felt more like a chana-aloo sabzi served with rice rather than a true biryani experience. The flavors could have been more layered and the dish better integrated.

Overall, Urban Tadka still offers a great meal with its vibrant starters and beverages — would love to return and try more dishes from their menu!

You can enjoy a calm and cosy evening here with friends and family, they have good punjabi food options in both veg and non veg and they serve alcohol as well.

Booked a table via the district app and paid 50 rs extra, It saved 350+ on the overall bill

We totally loved this concept, something which bought our memories back.

I must say the place was lively, packed with energy, and had a great playlist that kept the mood upbeat all evening. Service was smooth despite the crowd, and the staff was warm and attentive., Specially Amar, he was a great server and ensured we had a great time, loved his recommendation on food.

The food was flavorful and well-curated!! The highlights for us were the Veg Himalayan Thukpa, Dosh Momo, and Paneer Cheese Kebab.
And yes the must must try cocktails taking inspiration from old Bombay, it completely stole the show — “Oh My Darling” and “LIC” are a must-try. They’re inventive, well-balanced, and absolutely worth it, also the Sobo Snob, I loved it.

Permit and Co. isn’t just a place to eat and drink, it’s a vibe, total nostalgic with their food menu and chakhnas to pair with. ["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹600–800, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 weeks ago, review=Having lived and worked in Japan, albeit many moons ago, I was not expecting to be reminded of the tastes and feel of a typical izakaya in the land of the rising sun, in, of all places, Bandra, Mumbai.
We were ushered to our seating by a raucous welcome from the Kuuraku staff, which was more reminiscent of the Wankhede Stadium than a Japanese restaurant. But there was a effervescence about the staff at Kuuraku, reflecting the confidence that they have in their excellent food.
We ordered the Special Kushi Course, comprising 5 sticks of yakitori. The standout of this was the chicken tail. It was so good that we ordered two extra sticks of this, named bonjiri shio. We also ordered a portion of pork belly yakitori although this was very slightly disappointing as it was a little on the tough side. Another slight disappointment was the chargrilled asparagus wrapped in pork belly. Again, the pork belly wasn't as tender as I expected and the asparagus was a little small and fibrous. However, the edamame challenge was a lot of fun. The idea is to grab as much edamame as possible with one hand - and what you grab is what you get to eat. I used my goalkeeper hands to grab, what the server told me was an over par amount. The edamame was quite good too. The crunchy ebi roll was very generous too coming as a generous portion. The temperature of the rice was spot on as was the consistency. Could the quality of the rice be higher as in Japan? Well yes if you can get that rice but otherwise it really was excellent. The same goes for the pork rice. Here the consistency or the stickiness of the rice was more important than in the ebi roll and if they could get better rice it was be amazing. The slight disappointment was the inclusion of bell peppers. Heresy! Finally, the tea was served in a beautiful black pot, again, very true to Japan.
All in all this was an excellent place with a really true feel of Japan, helped also by the constant stream of Japanese music and the service was particularly excellent. 8/12 is my parents anniversary and exactly a year ago we arrived at Nara only to be turned away due to a staff party. One more attempt in between and it was fully booked.

This time i had booked the table only to be sure to have a table. There is outdoor seating too.

The hostess quick in finding our reservation and within seconds we were ushered into the restaurant and offered to choose our table which was a big plus as some places designate tables. The ambience was welcoming and elegant.

Our server Leishi arrived at our table with greetings and a smile to ask if we were comfortable. Within minutes, we had the menus in our hands and as usual i turned to our server, Leishi for recommendations. I never thought we’d end up having a five course dinner here. The recommendations offered by her were all worth a try. Although, the crispy lotus root starter that we wanted was sold out, we were happy choosing the crispy tofu dish instead. The thai ice tea was also unavailable. We chose a thai bubble tea instead. Do ask them to make a dish less spicy, not everyone can handle that kinda thai heat. Our soup, salad and starters arrived fairly quickly and were served well by Leishi. The chicken starter was a fantastic recommendation. The smoky flavour was also a bit like parmesan somehow and it was perfectly cooked.

For the mains, as recommended, we went for the house speciality, green curry with jasmine rice. For me, i got a chicken side dish to go with an extra portion of jasmine rice. I was full but something about the dish made me finish it to the last bit. It was delicious to say the least.

Time for dessert and we thought of skipping it because we were so full! But no! Lets get the sweet potato icecream with sticky rice. 2 scoops resting on sticky rice with some garnish. All gone in minutes. Well recommended by another server.

All in all, we had 5 courses we never thought we’d have. The food was truly authentic with great presentation elevated by some great service. I was very happy at the end.

I will return to try out the unavailable items and many more. Though, I would be on the lookout for some dine-out discounts on swiggy/zomato.

A big thanks to Leishi and other staff that interacted with us. Your warmth and smiles truly made our (parent’s) anniversary dinner exxtra special.

This one will be remembered.

Loved the dessert, must try and highly recommended! And towards the end we were presented with a platter of paan - Meetha (Sweet) and Saada (Plain). Couldnt have asked for more!

Younion season 2 is something you shouldn't miss out on.

Younion has more than 300 shots and 25 variety of new cocktails at an affordable rates on their menu for your gang. The ambiance of this place is characterized by its open air kitchen and it's enticing canopy. The Spanish and Italian folk music playing in the background incites feelings of cravings and euphoria. The place is embellished with an amazing set up in the dining area with spacious seating. On top of that, the dessert bar with an amazing line up of sweet treats and confectionery adds to the charm.

The bistro makes you feel in your element with their camaraderie. The atmosphere of this place and the crew connive to make the customer feel like a huésped as they embrace them to their ménage.

The service was pretty good. Our table was hosted by Mr. Rahul, Mr. Nikhil and Mr. Vishal. They helped us out in selecting the dishes and were very friendly. The restaurant being an part of The Empresa, has to manage the hotel guests along with the adventurous diners who visit the place. So it may take a while to get what you order but the food is totally worth the wait.

They serve a variety of dishes from the Mediterranean and North Indian Cuisine. The menu is pretty elaborate and covers a lot of palatable dishes with top class presentation. The chefs collude to serve appetizing and innovative dishes to appease the diners and bring a smile of satisfaction on their faces.

Our table was festooned with salads, burgers, appetizers, risotto and desserts.
We started off with 'Feta & Co. '. It's a salad constructed with the Greek Feta and a combination of fresh fruits and mixed greens. The salty and tangy taste of Feta combined with the flavours of fresh fruits and avocado makes it one of the finest salads in the menu.

The 'Supreme Crisp Burger' had the perfect cohesiveness between the amount of bun, meat and toppings. It was a merger of the chicken supreme patty, onion rings with the side of potato wedges. The bun was nicely toasted to hold up the patty. The quality of the meat used was top class which made the burger very juicy.
We also had 'Easy green Burger' which was served with a side of potato wedges and salads. It had a delectable taste.

Mediterranean food is more than just pizza and spaghetti, for a change, we ordered 'Grilled Portobello & Asparagus Risotto'. It was ambrosial! Amazing taste. The 'Potato Mille-Feuille' was very appetizing. The combination of fried potatoes and wild mushrooms with parmesan ragoût made it delicious!

I’m sure the food at Papas Bombay is excellent. But great food doesn’t excuse poor customer handling, and that’s where they truly fell short.

Overview
AER at the Four Seasons is a rooftop experience that lives up to the hype. Perched high above Worli, it delivers sweeping Mumbai skyline and sea views, a modern yet warm ambience, and consistently polished service — ideal for both special evenings and relaxed drinks with friends.

Ambience & design
- Incredible vantage point: panoramic views of Mumbai and the Arabian Sea are the star — especially dramatic when clouds roll in or the city lights up at night.
- Roof engineering: the covered rooftop feels state-of-the-art — thoughtfully designed to shelter guests during rain while preserving the sense of openness. Even in a downpour the space felt airy and comfortable, with rain adding to the drama rather than disrupting the experience.
- Vibe: stylish, contemporary décor with an upscale lounge energy. Music, lighting and layout encourage both intimate conversations and lively groups without feeling crowded.

Drinks
- Negroni: expertly executed — perfectly blanched (clean, balanced bitterness and bright aromatics), with excellent temperature and presentation. The cocktail showcased strong technique and attention to classic proportions.
- Cocktail program: creative but respectful of classics; bartenders clearly know their craft and tailor drinks to taste.

Food
- Guacamole prepared tableside: a highlight. Watching it made fresh added theatre, and the result was vibrant, aromatic and packed with flavour — creamy texture, bright citrus and just the right seasoning. Superb balance of richness and acidity.
- Overall tasting: dishes leaned modern, high-quality and well-seasoned. Portions are geared for sharing and designed to complement the cocktail-led experience.

Service
- Attentive and professional without being intrusive. Staff handled the evening smoothly, from timing of drinks and food to accommodating the rain cover without fuss.
- Knowledgeable servers and bartenders willing to recommend pairings and adjust drinks to preference.

Pros
- Unmatched views and rooftop atmosphere.
- Weather-proofed design that keeps the rooftop enjoyable even in rain.
- High-caliber cocktails and memorable live-prep elements (e.g., guacamole).
- Polished, thoughtful service.

Cons / notes
- Popularity means it can get busy; reservations are recommended for prime seating.
- Price point is upscale — expect to pay a premium for the location and experience.

Who it’s for
- Couples seeking a romantic, skyline-backed evening.
- Groups celebrating special occasions.
- Cocktail enthusiasts who appreciate skilled bartending and well-executed classics.

Bottom line
AER at the Four Seasons is a standout rooftop destination in Mumbai. Chang’s at Lower Parel is one of those places you walk into with a certain set of expectations — especially for dinner. Big space, familiar menu, and that promise of bold Asian flavours. Our visit was mostly enjoyable, but a few things definitely held it back from being a great meal.

Let’s start with the biggest issue of the night — temperature. A surprising number of dishes arrived almost cold. Not “could be hotter” warm, but genuinely needing to be sent back. We had to request reheating more than once, which took away from the flow of the meal. For a restaurant of this scale and reputation, that was disappointing and honestly shouldn’t happen.

Drinks came first. The Samurai Fizz (2.5/5) was… fine. Refreshing, yes, but pretty forgettable. It didn’t really stand out in flavour. On the other hand, the Passionfruit Iced Tea (4.5/5) was excellent — well-balanced, refreshing, and easily the best drink we ordered.

Soups were a letdown. Both the Hot & Sour Soup (2/5) and Chang’s Noodle Soup (2/5) lacked depth and warmth — in flavour and temperature. They felt rushed and flat, which is a shame because these are usually comforting starters.

Things picked up once the appetisers started rolling in. The Shrimp Tempura Roll (4/5) was nicely done — crispy shrimp, clean flavours, and well-balanced textures. The Pan Fried Handmade Shrimp Dumplings (2/5), however, were underwhelming. Soft, yes, but bland and missing that punch you expect from dumplings.

Vegetarian dishes did surprisingly well. The Kung Pao Potatoes (4/5) were addictive — crispy, spicy, and full of flavour. Easily one of the better plates on the table.

Among the chicken dishes, both the Orange Chicken (4/5) and Dynamite Chicken (4/5) delivered what you expect — crispy, saucy, and comforting. No complaints there. But the real star of the night was the Ring of Fire Shrimp (5/5). Perfectly crispy, bold flavours, and just the right amount of heat. This dish alone made the wait and reheating worth it.

The Mongolian Tenderloin (3/5) was a mixed experience. The meat was beautifully tender, cooked just right, but the flavour was surprisingly bland. It needed more sauce or seasoning to really shine.

For sides, the Hong Kong Egg Fried Rice (4/5) was simple and satisfying, and the Chicken in Black Bean (4/5) was solid — comforting, flavourful, and reliable.

Desserts wrapped things up nicely. The Great Wall of Chocolate (4/5) was rich and indulgent without being too heavy, while the Banana Spring Roll (4/5) was crisp, warm, and a crowd-pleaser.

Where P.F. Chang’s really scored was service. The staff was extremely friendly, attentive, and handled the reheating requests politely and efficiently. They genuinely tried to make the experience better, which made a big difference. The atmosphere was pleasant — lively but not chaotic — making it a comfortable place for a dinner outing.

Overall, P.F. Chang’s Lower Parel had some strong dishes and excellent service, but the repeated issue of food being served cold brought the overall experience down. If they can fix that one major flaw, it would easily be a much better dining spot.
